featured_reviews.name: vikrant mandiya
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is one of the original budhhist relic that survived today in modern India.

Built somewhere around 2 BCE....with just lime, bricks , stone n mud ..it's shows the peak of support what buddhism enjoyed in that era...today standing n ruin with maximum neglect from the concerned parties.

Still standing tall in the densely populated sub of palghar.

featured_reviews.name: Cedric Noronha
featured_reviews.review_text: An ancient Buddhist Stupa located at Nalasopara-Nirmal Road in Nalasopara. It was built around 3rd century BC during the Ashokan era and is maintained by ASI. This Stupa houses Buddha sculptures, circular platforms etc. There is a half buried pillar signifying that Gautam Buddha had visited this place. However, it is still not maintained properly. During monsoon, this Stupa is covered in blue plastic sheet. There is an entrance gate and a statue of Gautam Buddha a little further away from the actual entrance. Had admired the ancient site and posed for photographs as a college student. It is an ideal place for those who are interested in history.

featured_reviews.name: vivek puthran
featured_reviews.review_text: There's not much to say about a 2000 year old site. You have to come to this place and soak it in. You will get the vibes that you are standing amidst something really grand and beautiful.  You don't come across something as old as this. You have to make the effort to come to it. If you are into covering the ancient caves of Maharashtra  / Mumbai then this one should definitely be on your to do list 👍

featured_reviews.name: Greeshma Gowda
featured_reviews.review_text: The stupa is currently under repair so avoid going there now. The ruins are in the middle of a well maintained garden. You can take a shared auto from nallasopara train station to this site. While returning we had to wait for some time to catch an auto.

featured_reviews.name: 39 Pratingya Jena
featured_reviews.review_text: Nothing much to see....just some structures.....only visit during some function otherwise waste of time

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Once a settlement for local tribes, this site was excavated to reveal four types of stupa combined in one.  Our expert guides from Bhovara Tours gave us an immersive history in a nutshell.  It is possible that the Buddha himself visited this site (pre stupa) and that the stupa was one of the many built under the aegis of Emperor Ashoka.

Relics found within are now displayed in the Bombay Museum in Fort.

A haven of tranquil green and a place of quiet contemplation - the stupa is situated within a grove of palm trees - a parikrama brings instant peace.

featured_reviews.name: Ramya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
The fort was built by the British East India company between 1867-1869. The fort was mainly built as a watch tower to look after the thane salt pans, it is still visible from the topmost point. The fort is not that well maintained, the stairs are broken but manageable. If you are going with family or alone, make sure to go before 11 am or in the evening by 5pm. The view is absolutely amazing.

It's believed that the tiles used for the fort were mangalorean tiles but it's no longer available. You can ignore the couple's sitting in the fort. Currently, only the rooms, well and pillars are there.

How to reach?
1. Get down at GTB or Sion station and move towards road number 1
There is no entrance fee

featured_reviews.name: Md Mahyuddin
featured_reviews.review_text: Very nice tourist place, full on weekends, great skyline view of mumbai, 10 min walking distance from sion railway station, small trek, no tickets, just go and enjoy.

featured_reviews.name: ravi sampat
featured_reviews.review_text:
WHY SHOULD ONE GO TO SION FORT?
SIon fort has lot to offer
1) for locals - a get together spot in lap of nature to do yoga, walk, exercise like climbing running etc.
2) for mumbaikar - an unknown heritage site which gives you a peak into ancient architecture and impress your guest from outside the city
3) for visitor to Mumbai - not to be missed by heritage lovers, as it has remains of a fort - a canon , multiple dilapidated rooms, a possible water tank
for all of above, the views from Sion fort of Mumbai landscape is going to stun you. You can view the 360 degree Mumbai skyline from Navi Mumbai to Bandra Worli Sealink to Thane Bhandup creek all from one spot. Undoubtedly Sunrise and Sunset are worth the visit.
The place is restored and made into a open gym with various equipment's provided (Kudos to BMC) , landscaped garden, Rest rooms, filtered water provision and jogging trail
I was here for first time on 25 feb 2024 and should have been here much earlier in my life is what I were my first thoughts. I walked down with 7 kg backpack as practice to my big climb coming up & it was worth my time as it has a share of small trek as well.
This place has some surprisingly beautiful spots for photo shoots. (See my video till end)

HOW TO REACH
Located at Sion East. 15 minutes walk from Sion station on central Mumbai local railway line, 30 minutes walk from Chunnabhati stataion on Harbour Mumbai local railway line . You can take taxi at almost minimum fares from both railway station. There is enough provision for parking for private vehicles
Multiple  BEST BUSES including AC BUSES also stop near this place. Ask for Sion fort or sion east station bus stop

featured_reviews.name: Meenal Anaokar
featured_reviews.review_text:
History in the city to explore.. Sion Fort. Half day tour.. for some spectacular views of Mumbai City from the top.
Walkable distance from Sion Railway station and Bus Depot. No entry fees. The fort is now under ASI department so well maintained. Dates back for Portuguese era who gave the 7 islands of Mumbai as dowry during Princess Catherina's to British Prince. You can also check and plan to watch Sunrise (Wadala n Creekside) and also Sunset (Dadar & Bandra Sealing side). Monsoon time, the greenery is soothing. Do visit and do reply to let me know your experience

featured_reviews.name: Joshua Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Built in 1800 by the North Salsette Society's local Taluka Board, this well was buried under debris and subsequent road developments, lost for years. It was rediscovered in 2018 with the efforts of local water conservationist Vincy Pareira and renovated in 2020 with the support of local corporator Tejasvee Ghosalkar. The mural sculpture depicting the culture and traditions of a typical East Indian village is designed by artists Sachin Waikar and Santosh Waikar.
